Restore standard folders resets their names, order and automatic assignments. Your own folders and their members stay. Reset all also removes your own folders and sorts installed mods into the standard folders. Category settings, enabled mods and load order stay unchanged. Save keeps this draft; Undo can reverse it.

Categories guide Auto-Sort. The standard order is recommended. Libraries, server administration, tile and model resources and maps come first; content is divided into building/crafting, survival/health, traits/skills, NPCs/creatures, audio/media, vehicles, clothing/appearance, weapons, visuals/animations and interface mods, with patches/addons afterwards.

Detection uses author categories, names, Mod IDs, map folders and a few reviewed exceptions. Steam Workshop tags are not read. Visuals covers world graphics, effects and animations; clothing/appearance packs stay in Clothing. Server & administration covers management tools and spawn protection, not every multiplayer-compatible mod. Unknown or mixed-purpose mods stay in Content. Your manual category assignment overrides automatic detection. QoL is a separate overlapping label, not a sorting category.

Open Categories to create custom categories, rename categories, inspect members or move categories earlier/later. Mark mods in the main screen and use Assign selection. Use automatic removes their manual assignment. Only custom categories can be deleted; their mods return to automatic detection.

Changes stay in a draft until saved. Undo can reverse draft edits and the last saved category change. Reset standards restores standard names/order and automatic assignments while keeping custom categories and members. Reset all also removes custom categories and manual assignments. Folder layouts stay separate. Run Auto-Sort afterwards to apply the preferred category order to your active mods.

Mouse and keyboard:
- Click to select; Ctrl-click marks individual mods and Shift-click selects a range.
- Checkboxes toggle activation; stars manage favorites. Double-clicking a mod name also toggles activation.
- Drag list handles to change active order or assign installed mods to folders. Escape cancels dragging.
- Escape closes the current dropdown or dialog before leaving its parent screen.

Controller in Mods:
- Mods opens directly in the installed list. LB/RB cycles through installed mods, active load order, the right-hand information pane, Accept and Back. A on Accept saves and returns; A on Back cancels selection changes. Navigation alone changes nothing.
- B closes the current menu/dialog and returns straight to the originating pane. In a main pane it cancels the Mods session; it does not save a draft.
- A marks/unmarks mods or a package. Moving through the list keeps your marks.
- X opens selection actions: enable/disable, folders, groups/notes and rules.
- Y opens combinable filters for the installed list. Up/Down only moves the cursor; A toggles a filter. RB focuses Clear filters, A clears them, and LB returns to the first filter.
- In the active load order, Y picks up marked active mods, or the focused mod if none are marked. Up/Down chooses the insertion gap. A or Y places them; B cancels the move. X cancels the move and opens selection actions. Their relative order is preserved, and Undo reverses the drop.
- L3 toggles favorites for the mod or package under the cursor without marking it. If you marked mods with A, it applies to that selection.
- R3 opens view switches for mod grouping and folders. Each switch is saved; B returns to your pane. Groups and notes remain in the X action menu.
- Left/Right closes/opens folders and packages.
- Menu opens editing actions for your pane: folders, groups, search and filters on the left; Auto-Sort, rules, categories and Undo in the active order; selection actions and Workshop links on the right. Presets have their own submenu in either mod list. Tools, including Help, remain available in every pane. View switches stay on R3. Closing an editor returns to the same pane.
- In the right-hand pane, Left selects Details and Right selects Dependencies. Up/Down browses entries; A opens a link or selects a dependency.
- Text fields use the game's on-screen keyboard.

In help, choose a topic above or use Previous/Next. Focus the text panel with A and scroll with the directional controls; B returns to the help controls. Close or Escape returns to the screen you opened help from.

Right-click a mod or folder for its actions. Right-clicking an already marked mod keeps your selection; choosing an unmarked mod selects it alone. The same mod and folder actions remain available through the normal controller buttons and editors. Tools opens reports, previous lists and personal backups.

Small i buttons beside the main pane headers show guidance on hover. Click one or press A to open its help topic. Ordinary rows stay quiet; pause over shortened text to read it in full.

Button hints and the controller focus border appear only during controller use and hide when you use the mouse or keyboard. Directional hints use the matching D-pad arrows. They use the game's controller icons where available.

Select a mod to open Details on the right. Description, preview, author, version, Mod ID and Workshop information appear here. Path / Workshop URL shows the local source or Workshop address; available links can be opened directly.

Workshop package size, update/publication dates and installed component counts are shown when available. Size belongs to the whole Workshop package, not one component's installed disk usage. Local mods and unavailable online data show Not available.

Dependencies shows what the mod requires and which active mods depend on it. Review this before disabling a library or base mod. The manager previews affected active addons, including indirect dependents.

Components are grouped by their shared Workshop ID. Grouping does not mean every component must be enabled, or that similar names are automatically exclusive alternatives.

Category detection explains whether the assignment comes from you, mod metadata, an exact reviewed Mod ID, map directories or the name/ID. For active mods, Load order shows relevant order rules and addon recommendations; a skipped recommendation is marked as such.

Folders organize the installed list; they do not change activation or load order. Open Folders to create, rename or delete folders and manage their members. Each mod can belong to one folder. Deleting a folder leaves its mods installed and returns them to Without folder.

Select one or several mods, open Folders, choose the destination and move the selection there. The + beside a mod opens this editor; the + beside a package or reviewed family selects all its installed components, including members currently in other folders. Select whole package also reunites a split package.

Drag the handles at the far left to move a mod, marked selection or package onto a folder. A closed folder can receive a drop. Drop on Without folder to remove the assignment. Drag folder handles to reorder folders. Assignment saves immediately and the main Undo reverses the last drop.

Starting folders use your categories once. Later category edits do not overwrite the layout; newly installed mods remain without a folder until assigned. Reset can restore standard folders and improved automatic assignments while keeping your own folders and members, or remove all own folders. Editor changes and resets stay in a draft until saved; Undo or Discard changes reverses the draft.

Groups are personal labels for things such as server requirements, vehicles or mods to test. Unlike folders, a mod can belong to several groups. Groups do not set load order or edit categories.

Mark mods in the main list and open Groups & notes. Select a group to see its members; selecting it does not add mods. Use Add selection to add the marked mods, or mark members and remove them. Creating a group includes the current selection. Groups also work as filters.

Notes belong to individual mods. Select a main-list mod or group member to edit its note, then save. Search also finds your notes.

An exclusive group marks alternatives: at most one member should be active. It is not a pairwise on/off switch; a group may contain three or more alternatives, and all may be disabled. Activation previews show conflicting active alternatives and their affected addons.

Save keeps group/note edits and leaves the editor open with Close. Editing again changes this to Discard changes. Closing an unsaved draft discards it; separately saved groups and notes remain after Back from Mods.

Map Order controls priority where maps overlap: higher entries win over lower entries. It is available for a selected world even without overlaps. It is separate from the order of Mod IDs.

Auto-Sort uses declared map relationships to put overlays before their base maps. An existing Muldraugh, KY entry moves last; it is never added to a standalone world. Unknown priorities keep their relative order where possible.

Overlaps lists the game's overlap reports with current priority numbers. An overlap is not automatically an error. Choose which map should win when there is no known instruction. Sorting cannot merge two maps replacing the same cell.

Reset restores the order from when this window opened; Undo reverses the last sort or reset. Accept keeps the displayed map order, while Back leaves without accepting it. Escape returns to Mods after closing any open dialog first.

New saves your current selection and load order as a preset under a new name. Save preset saves the current setup under the chosen name; Delete preset removes the selected preset. Saving a preset does not apply it to your active list.

Choosing a preset opens a checked replacement preview. Select the source preset on the right, then use Apply preview to update your selection. Preview merge keeps your current mods and adds the source. The left list is a comparison reference; the actual effect on your current selection is shown separately. Required dependencies and missing mods are shown before applying. Apply is available immediately for a valid preview; blocking reasons appear in the list. Use the main Accept button afterwards to save and apply the selection.

Export preset shares selection/order as text or a file. Select export text and press Ctrl+C, or use Copy preset for the full text. Import preset accepts pasted text or a file, previews its contents and saves a named preset. Importing does not subscribe, download or enable mods.

Known Workshop IDs are included in shared presets. Select a linked entry to open its Workshop page, or copy missing-package links. Older shares without these IDs still work, but cannot provide missing links. Personal folders, categories, rules, groups and notes stay on your PC.

To transfer your personal layout and rules as well, use the separate personal backup under Tools. Preset sharing remains limited to the mod list and its known Workshop links.

Problems brings missing requirements, declared incompatibilities and conflicting or violated load-order rules together. Click an affected entry to reveal the mod and inspect its relationships. The manager can only check relationships that are declared or known; it cannot prove that arbitrary mods are compatible.

A local mod and a subscribed Workshop copy may coexist. This is a source note, not a blocking conflict; the game chooses which copy loads. Duplicate IDs in the active ordered list are a different issue and must be resolved.

Open Tools → Check report when asking for help. It includes game/ModOrderPlus versions, the active load order with known Workshop IDs and detected problems. The text can be selected or copied with Copy report. Personal installation paths, private notes and account details are omitted.

An update marker is not a conflict warning. If a requirement is missing, install the required mod and check again. Review a mod author's instructions when its required order is not recorded in metadata.

Recorded Lua errors also appear here and in Needs attention when their first non-built-in Lua frame identifies exactly one installed Mod ID or name. The entry shows a script basename and line, without storing the full trace. Repeated locations are combined. Errors without a unique source remain unassigned; caller mods further down a stack are not blamed. These are warnings from the current game run, may predate later mod changes, and never block sorting, presets or Accept. Refresh Problems to collect new entries. The existing game error buffer is read within fixed limits; large log files are not scanned. Missing translations and generic asset warnings are not treated as Lua mod errors.

Open Tools → Previous mod lists to review the last five lists kept before saving a changed selection or order. History is separate for the general list, new-game setup, each existing save and each identified Host server. An unidentified server never shares another server’s history.

Choose a previous list to see which mods would be enabled, disabled or moved, and whether map order changes. Missing mods or conflicting requirements/rules block restoration. Restore stages the list for review; Undo reverses it, Back cancels it, and Save selection in Review changes saves it. Accept in Mods saves and returns to the previous menu. Favorites stay as they are. A history entry is a previous mod list, not a backup of a mod’s files or your world.

Tools → Personal settings backup saves folders/view settings, categories/assignments, custom rules/priorities, groups and notes to a .mopbackup file in Zomboid/Lua. To receive a backup, place it there, enter its filename, select the areas to restore and choose Preview file. The preview shows the actual changed entries. Restore replaces the chosen areas, including removing entries absent from the backup. Unchecked areas, mod selection, presets and Workshop update history are preserved.

Personal restoration saves immediately and does not activate or sort mods. Before restoring, a recovery file named ModOrderPlus_before_restore.mopbackup is verified. Preview that file to reverse a restoration. An interrupted restoration is resumed before either personal settings store loads.

Backups include personal notes. Share them only if you want to include those notes. Existing different backup files are not overwritten; choose another filename.

Click a mod to select it. Its checkbox or the Enable/Disable action changes activation; double-clicking the name also toggles it. The star controls favorites.

Use Ctrl-click to mark individual mods and Shift-click for a range. With several marked mods, Selection actions opens a shared Enable/Disable preview. Check required dependencies, conflicting alternatives and affected addons, then apply or close it. Favorite actions affect the marked selection too.

Review changes lists enabled, disabled and reordered mods. Undo an individual change or use the main Undo action to reverse the latest supported edit. Close keeps your staged mod-selection edits; Discard all reverts them. Save selection keeps the Mods screen open. Accept in Mods finishes editing and returns to the previous menu.

Back from Mods cancels the selection session. Rules, presets, categories, folders, groups and notes that you saved separately stay saved.

After Save selection, Back discards only later edits. The game applies the saved list when you leave Mods.

When you open Mods through Host, Accept saves the selection to that server's settings. A dedicated server does not need ModOrderPlus itself; it is a client-side menu tool.

Export for server is available in Mod Order. Copy the current configuration lines or save them to Zomboid\Lua\ModOrderPlus_export.ini in your user folder. Copy the lines into your dedicated server configuration yourself; exporting does not rewrite that configuration.

Mods= preserves the current Mod IDs and order, including local mods. WorkshopItems= includes each known Workshop download ID once, even if the package contains several mods. Missing Workshop IDs are reported; a local mod's published package can be recognized when its ID is known.

Map= uses the accepted map order when one world can be identified. If map information is unavailable or several separate worlds are enabled, it is omitted with a note. Choose or keep the server world yourself. Check the exported lines before starting the server.

The active list shows the actual load order. Drag its handles to insert mods elsewhere. Marked active mods move together in their existing relative order. An insertion marker and edge scrolling help with long lists; Undo reverses the move.

Auto-Sort uses required dependencies, author before/after instructions, your saved rules and known addon relationships. Categories arrange the remaining mods where possible. Explicit requirements and order rules take priority; sorting cannot make incompatible mods compatible.

For a custom rule, select the mod and open Rules. Choose This mod loads BEFORE or This mod loads AFTER, then click target mods in the existing load-order list. The direction refers to the mod named in the panel. Click a target again to remove its rule. Changing direction replaces the opposite custom rule for that pair.

Save changes keeps the rule draft. Earlier/later priority is optional and remains subordinate to dependencies and rules. Reset can clear one mod's custom rules/priority or all custom preferences; mod requirements and included known relationships remain. Saving a rule or category does not itself run Auto-Sort. In Mod Order, Accept keeps the displayed order. Back may ask whether to keep changes; choose No to leave without applying that window's order edits.

After Auto-Sort, Review changes explains the category source and relationships considered for each moved mod. Category and priority preferences only choose between mods whose requirements and preceding rules have already been satisfied.

Enable ModOrderPlus and restart the game. Open Mods to manage your installed collection and active load order together. Smaller screens use tabs for the two lists.

Choose your mods, use Auto-Sort if needed and check the result. Accept saves the selection for the menu you came from: the main menu, a new game, a saved game or Host. Back cancels the selection changes.

Use the topic selector above or Previous and Next below to explore this help. Closing the help returns to your current screen without changing your setup.

ModOrderPlus is a client-side menu tool for Build 42.20 and later. Mods themselves still need to support your game version. Disable Mod Load Order Sorter and its extensions before using ModOrderPlus.

Search matches mod names, Mod IDs, Workshop IDs and your notes. Combine filters, for example a vehicle folder with disabled mods, or QoL with favorites. Remove a filter through its x or open Active filters to inspect and clear the selection.

Filters combine across different types. Choosing active replaces inactive; another folder replaces the previous folder. The active list always shows the full load order.

Show folders and Group mods are independent switches at the top right. Both start enabled and remember your choice. Mods from the same Workshop package are grouped together. Reviewed families, such as KR SolarOS and its Fuel/Lights addons, can also group separate downloads. Similar names alone never create a family. Expanded groups show branches beside their individual mods. Groups stay within their assigned folders; switch off Show folders to see the combined group across folders.

QoL matches explicit QoL or Quality of Life labels; it can overlap with any category. Updated marks Workshop packages with a newer update date than your previous recorded visit. The first successful check establishes a baseline. Offline or failed checks do not create update markers.

A stacked-tile symbol identifies each expandable mod group. When expanded, its member lines connect directly to the symbol; mod icons stay beside it.
